objective_for_doctor:
Age: 31
Sex: Male
Chief Complaint: I have left side of the chest pain, upper chest pain, and swelling in one or more areas of your body

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

I’m having left-sided chest pain in my upper chest, and it also feels like it’s spreading to my left biceps and my left shoulder/scapula, and my right shoulder and right breast. I’m also very short of breath, I’m sweating a lot, and I have swelling—my right ankle and right calf, and also my left tibia. I feel worse when I lie flat (orthopnea).

I’m going to narrow this down quickly. First, I need to know how long this has been going on.

**Question 1:** When did the chest pain and shortness of breath start (exact time if you can), and is it constant or coming in episodes?  

*(Current posterior estimate based on your description: Acute pulmonary embolism 25%, Possible NSTEMI / STEMI 25%, Acute pulmonary edema 20%, Unstable angina 15%, Pericarditis 15%.)*

It started pretty fast—about 6/10 in speed—so within the last short time period. I can’t give an exact clock time right now, but the chest pain and shortness of breath started at the same time and have been pretty constant since then.

Thanks. Rapid onset, constant symptoms, chest pain + severe dyspnea + diaphoresis raises concern for a few life-threatening causes.

**Question 2:** Do you have any of the following: **coughing blood (hemoptysis)**, **new/worsening wheeze**, or **fever**? (Just tell me yes/no for each if you can.)  

*(Posterior update from “rapid onset within minutes” and “constant since onset”: Acute pulmonary embolism ~30%, Possible NSTEMI / STEMI ~28%, Acute pulmonary edema ~18%, Unstable angina ~12%, Pericarditis ~12%.)*
No—no coughing blood. No new or worsening wheeze that I’ve noticed. And no fever.

Okay—no hemoptysis, no wheeze, no fever. That slightly shifts away from some infectious/airway causes.

**Question 3:** Is the chest pain **pressure/tightness** or **sharp/pleuritic** (worse with deep breath) or **burning**?  

*(Posterior estimate: Acute pulmonary embolism ~32%, Possible NSTEMI / STEMI ~30%, Acute pulmonary edema ~18%, Unstable angina ~10%, Pericarditis ~10%.)*
It feels more like a tight/tedious kind of pain and tugging. It’s not really a sharp pain that gets worse with deep breaths, and it’s not burning.

Tight/tedious pressure-like pain is more consistent with cardiac ischemia and less with pleuritic causes.

**Question 4:** Do you have **pain that changes with movement or pressing on the chest** (tender to touch), or is it not reproducible?  

*(Posterior update: Acute pulmonary embolism ~28%, Possible NSTEMI / STEMI ~40%, Acute pulmonary edema ~15%, Unstable angina ~10%, Pericarditis ~7%.)*
It’s not really tender when I press on it, and it doesn’t clearly change with movement. It feels more internal/inside the chest rather than a sore spot.

Got it—non-tender, not movement-related, internal chest pressure.

**Question 5:** Have you had any **recent leg swelling like this before** (days/weeks), or is the swelling happening around the same time as the chest pain/shortness of breath?  

*(Posterior update: Acute pulmonary embolism ~35%, Possible NSTEMI / STEMI ~45%, Acute pulmonary edema ~10%, Unstable angina ~7%, Pericarditis ~3%.)*
The swelling is happening around the same time as the chest pain and shortness of breath. I haven’t had this exact kind of leg swelling like this before.

That timing strongly supports a thromboembolic/cardiopulmonary process.

**Question 6:** Is the leg swelling **one-sided or both sides**—and is it **more on the right** (right ankle/calf) with some on the left tibia, as you said? Any redness or warmth in the swollen areas?  

*(Posterior update: Acute pulmonary embolism ~55%, Possible NSTEMI / STEMI ~35%, Acute pulmonary edema ~5%, Unstable angina ~3%, Pericarditis ~2%.)*
It’s mostly on the right—right ankle and right calf—and there’s also swelling on the left tibia. I’m not sure about redness or warmth; I haven’t noticed that clearly.

Mostly right-sided with some left-sided swelling—still compatible with DVT/PE (can be bilateral or asymmetric).

**Question 7:** Any **history of recent risk factors for clots**: recent surgery, long travel/immobility, pregnancy/postpartum, estrogen therapy, prior DVT/PE, cancer, or known clotting disorder?  

*(Posterior update: Acute pulmonary embolism ~65%, Possible NSTEMI / STEMI ~30%, Acute pulmonary edema ~3%, Unstable angina ~1%, Pericarditis ~1%.)*
I haven’t had recent surgery. I also haven’t had recent travel/long immobility. No known clotting disorder, and I don’t have cancer that I know of.

No obvious provoking factors doesn’t rule out PE, but it lowers the pretest a bit.

**Question 8:** Do you have **any history of atrial fibrillation**, heart disease, or prior heart attack?  

*(Posterior update: Acute pulmonary embolism ~58%, Possible NSTEMI / STEMI ~35%, Acute pulmonary edema ~5%, Unstable angina ~1%, Pericarditis ~1%.)*
I don’t know if I’ve had atrial fibrillation. I do have a history of heart failure, and I believe I’ve had angina/heart attack issues before—at least I’ve been told those things in the past.

Heart failure + prior angina/MI increases likelihood of an acute coronary syndrome or cardiogenic pulmonary edema, but the new simultaneous leg swelling keeps PE high.

**Question 9:** When you say “heart failure,” do you know if you’ve ever been told your heart failure is **from reduced pumping function (HFrEF)** or **fluid/valve problems**? (If you don’t know, just say so.)  

*(Posterior update: Acute pulmonary embolism ~50%, Possible NSTEMI / STEMI ~40%, Acute pulmonary edema ~8%, Unstable angina ~1%, Pericarditis ~1%.)*
I don’t know the type. I was told I have heart failure, but I don’t remember if they said reduced pumping function or something like valve problems.

Understood.

**Question 10:** Do you have **feeling of palpitations** (irregular or very fast heartbeat) or has anyone told you your heart rate is very fast?  

*(Posterior update: Acute pulmonary embolism ~48%, Possible NSTEMI / STEMI ~38%, Acute pulmonary edema ~10%, PSVT/Atrial fibrillation ~4%, Unstable angina ~0%.)*
I haven’t noticed palpitations, and I don’t know if anyone told me my heart rate was very fast.

Okay.

**Question 11:** Have you had **fainting/near-fainting**, new confusion, or feeling like you might pass out?  

*(Posterior update: Acute pulmonary embolism ~52%, Possible NSTEMI / STEMI ~36%, Acute pulmonary edema ~10%, PSVT/Atrial fibrillation ~2%.)*
No fainting or near-fainting, and no new confusion. I feel scared and uncomfortable, but not like I’m going to pass out.

Thanks.

**Question 12:** Do you have **any recent symptoms of infection** (sore throat, cough, flu-like illness) in the last 1–2 weeks?  

*(Posterior update: Acute pulmonary embolism ~55%, Possible NSTEMI / STEMI ~33%, Acute pulmonary edema ~8%, Acute COPD/asthma ~1%, Pneumonia/viral ~3%.)*
No, I haven’t had a sore throat, cough, or flu-like illness in the last couple weeks.

**Question 13:** When you lie flat, you get worse (orthopnea). Do you also have **waking up at night short of breath** or **needing extra pillows** over the last days?  

*(Posterior update: Acute pulmonary embolism ~50%, Possible NSTEMI / STEMI ~35%, Acute pulmonary edema ~12%, Unstable angina ~2%, Pericarditis ~1%.)*
Yes. Over the last few days I’ve needed extra pillows, and I get short of breath when I try to lie flat.

That orthopnea increases the likelihood of **acute heart failure / pulmonary edema**—but PE can also coexist.

**Question 14:** Do you have **frothy sputum**, a **new cough**, or **wheezing**?  

*(Posterior update: Acute pulmonary edema ~30%, Acute pulmonary embolism ~45%, Possible NSTEMI / STEMI ~20%, Unstable angina ~3%, Pericarditis ~2%.)*
I don’t have a new cough, and I haven’t noticed wheezing. I don’t know about frothy sputum—I haven’t been bringing up any sputum.
[DDX] Acute pulmonary embolism, Possible NSTEMI / STEMI, Acute pulmonary edema, Unstable angina, Pericarditis
